solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Director replacing line in pretty funny play

indicators.note: replacing tells us one letter steps in for another in the word for pretty

parts.note: comely means pretty, attractive

explanation.surface: A director's tinkering with a line makes a play rather amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty funny' reads as 'quite funny', but 'pretty' is the word to be altered and 'funny play' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedy is a theatrical work written to amuse its audience.

clue.text: Pain mounting after 101 lashes

indicators.note: after places this piece behind the numeral

parts.note: CI is 101 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to ail is to pain or trouble

explanation.surface: A painful flogging of 101 lashes, as in a naval punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'lashes' look like strokes of a whip, but they are eyelashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cilia are eyelashes, and also the tiny hair-like projections on cells.

clue.text: Import last of files in seconds

parts.note: import in the sense of importance or significance is moment, as in 'of great moment'

indicators.note: last of picks out the final letter of files

parts.note: the final letter of files

explanation.surface: Bringing in the last of the files takes only seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Import' looks like a verb for bringing in data, but it is the noun meaning significance.
explanation.definitionFit: Seconds and moments are both very short spans of time, as in 'back in a second'.

clue.text: Pepys said to suffer indigestion

indicators.note: to suffer here is to be knocked about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: The famous diarist Samuel Pepys is reported to have had stomach trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Pepys was the seventeenth-century English diarist, famous for his food-filled entries.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspepsia is the medical term for indigestion, discomfort after eating.

clue.text: One's work initially is cliched and short-sighted

parts.note: one's, said by the speaker of themselves, is my
OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: the first letters of is and cliched

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses someone's work as hackneyed and lacking vision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short-sighted' looks like a criticism of the work's vision; it is the literal definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Myopic describes nearsightedness, and figuratively a lack of foresight.

clue.text: About to feed cattle and rabbits

indicators.note: to feed means to go into, so this letter is put inside the cattle

parts.note: yaks are long-haired Himalayan cattle

explanation.surface: A farmer is about to give fodder to cows and bunnies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbits' looks like the animals but is the British verb 'rabbit on', to chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit is British slang for talking at length, the same as to yack.

clue.text: Reportedly water-repellent bird

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard spoken, so the answer sounds like the two words

parts.note: to pee is to pass water, and foul means repellent, so this is heard as pee-foul

explanation.surface: A bird is said to have feathers that shed water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water-repellent' reads as waterproof, but it splits into urine and disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: The peafowl is the species of pheasant whose male is the peacock.

clue.text: Criminal pinching a Trojan horse's finery

indicators.note: pinching means holding tight, so the convict goes around the rest

parts.note: con is short for convict, a criminal
Paris was the Trojan prince who abducted Helen

explanation.surface: A thief steals the decorations from the Trojan horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trojan horse's' seems to belong together, but Trojan is Paris and horse's goes with finery.
explanation.definitionFit: A caparison is an ornamental cloth covering spread over a horse's saddle and harness.

clue.text: Part of problem is his fault

indicators.note: part of means the answer is a run of letters within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of problem, through is, into his

explanation.surface: Someone takes the blame for a problem, since it was partly his doing.
explanation.definitionFit: A blemish is a flaw or defect, a fault in something otherwise good.

clue.text: Ragged rear of malodorous pants

indicators.note: rear of picks the final letter of malodorous

parts.note: the final letter of malodorous
pants is British slang for rubbish, so crappy

explanation.surface: Torn, smelly underpants are worn ragged at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like the garment (British underpants), but here it is the slang adjective for poor quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrappy means untidy or disorganised, made of odds and ends, like something ragged.

clue.text: Half of Cubans backing racehorse that gets beaten

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the chosen letters are read from the end
half of the word is taken, here its second three letters

parts.note: Red Rum is a famous racehorse, three times winner of the Grand National

explanation.surface: Part of a group of Cuban punters putting their money on a horse that loses.
explanation.walkthrough: The last half of CUBANS is ANS, which 'backing' turns to SNA. 'that gets beaten' looks like describing the losing horse, but it defines the drum.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare drum is a percussion instrument played by striking it with sticks.

clue.text: Lenin wasn't playing game

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are messed about with, rearranged

explanation.surface: Lenin did not take part in a sporting match.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawn tennis is the formal name of the racket sport played on grass courts.

clue.text: Setters' occasional uncouthness riles some at first

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each word before it

parts.note: the first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A setter admits that crossword compilers are sometimes rude enough to annoy solvers.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves in the first person, so 'setters'' means belonging to us.
explanation.definitionFit: Ours is the possessive belonging to us, the setters speaking of themselves.

clue.text: Nanas heading off amorous advances

definitions.note: nana is British slang for a fool

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is cut away

parts.note: to make a pass is to make an amorous advance

explanation.surface: Grandmothers fend off unwanted flirtation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nanas' looks like grandmothers, but it is the British slang word for silly people.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nanas and asses are informal words for foolish people.

clue.text: Mixed our shandy without water

indicators.note: mixed means stirred up, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A barman prepares a shandy with no water added.
explanation.walkthrough: A shandy is beer mixed with lemonade, a popular British pub drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Anhydrous is the chemical term for a substance containing no water.

clue.text: Husband stifled by routine without becoming unfeeling

indicators.note: stifled by means smothered inside, so the husband goes within the other words

parts.note: a rut is a dull, fixed routine
less means without, as in 'less sugar'

explanation.surface: A husband trapped in a dull marriage grows cold and heartless.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruthless means having no pity or compassion for others.

clue.text: Actor and oddball are dating

indicators.note: oddball read as odd suggests the letters are in an odd, scrambled order

explanation.surface: A performer and an eccentric are going out together.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedian is an actor who specialises in tragic roles.

clue.text: I spy hard rum in dock

indicators.note: rum means strange, so the letters come out in an odd order

explanation.surface: A spy at the harbour spots strong liquor being smuggled ashore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the sailors' drink, but it is the adjective meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipyard is a place where ships are built and repaired, a kind of dockyard.

clue.text: Childish whimper stopped by Tudor queen

indicators.note: stopped by means plugged by, so the queen fills the middle of the whimper

parts.note: to pule is to whimper or whine
Elizabeth I, the Tudor queen, signed as ER I, Elizabeth Regina the First

explanation.surface: A child's crying is silenced by a stern Tudor monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Puerile means silly or immature, behaving like a child.

clue.text: Grey layer on sides of Agas

indicators.note: on means this piece comes next, after the outer letters
sides of takes the outer letters of Agas

parts.note: the first and last letters of Agas
a hen is a layer of eggs

explanation.surface: A grey coating forms on the edges of a kitchen range.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a heavy cast-iron range cooker found in many British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen describes a pale grey colour, like ash, especially of a face.

clue.text: One inheriting their mess after leaders ousted

indicators.note: leaders ousted means the first letter of their is dropped
after, read with leaders ousted, also applies to mess, so its first letter goes too

explanation.surface: Someone takes over the chaos left behind once the bosses have been thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: An heiress is a woman who inherits, or stands to inherit, property or wealth.

clue.text: Incisiveness of Heidegger regularly noted

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter, starting from the second

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of Heidegger

explanation.surface: A reader admires the sharp thinking of the German philosopher Heidegger.
explanation.definitionFit: Edge is sharpness or keenness, as in an edge to one's wit.

clue.text: Liberal luvvie led a variety show

indicators.note: liberal suggests a free treatment of the letters, which are rearranged

explanation.surface: A left-leaning theatrical type headed a variety performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks like the abbreviation L, but it is the anagram signal; a luvvie is British slang for a gushing actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaudeville was a theatrical entertainment of mixed song, dance and comic acts.

clue.text: Cellar clearance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an underground storage room
second meaning: a leap that clears an obstacle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cellar clearance' reads like emptying a basement; the words are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A vault is an underground chamber for storage, and also a jump over a barrier using hands or a pole.

clue.text: Clear clue uncovered by detectives

indicators.note: uncovered means the outer letters are stripped off, leaving the middle

parts.note: the two middle letters of clue
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police

explanation.surface: Police detectives expose an obvious clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucid means clearly expressed and easy to understand.

clue.text: Generous officer promises to pay

parts.note: a cop is a police officer
an IOU is a written promise to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A kind-hearted policeman offers to cover the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Copious means plentiful or abundant, as generous helpings are.

clue.text: Still seeing that entertaining lassie after vacation

indicators.note: entertaining means holding a guest, so the other letters sit inside

parts.note: since means seeing that, because

indicators.note: after vacation means emptied of its insides, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of lassie, its middle emptied

explanation.surface: A man is still courting a girl after the holidays are over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vacation' looks like a holiday, but it means emptying out; lassie is Scots for a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Still, as a noun, is quiet calm, as in the still of the night.

clue.text: Heartily kissing ex-PM in close-fitting dress

indicators.note: heartily takes the heart, the central letter, of kissing

parts.note: the central letter of the seven in kissing
Edward Heath was British Prime Minister from 1970 to 1974

explanation.surface: A former prime minister is caught passionately kissing someone in a tight dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath dress is a narrow, close-fitting dress that follows the body's shape.

clue.text: University students, extremely entitled and idle

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students in the UK

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so the first and last letters of entitled

parts.note: the first and last letters of entitled

explanation.surface: University students who feel very entitled and lazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Idle' looks like a description of the students, but it is the definition, meaning not in use.
explanation.definitionFit: Unused means idle in the sense of not being employed or put to work.
